exposure: pre-pregnancy BMI (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese)
cohort: The study included a total of 75,773 pregnant women registered between 2016 and 2020 in China.
finding: Underweight women demonstrated a lower risk of preeclampsia and severe preeclampsia, while overweight and obese women exhibited a higher occurrence of both preeclampsia and severe preeclampsia, regardless of maternal age.
